column1: judicious§Judicious use of white space does half the design's work.§**恰当**地留白就完成了设计一半的工作。
juxtapose§Juxtapose the two drafts and the editing becomes visible.§把两份草稿**并置**，编辑的痕迹就显现了。
juxtaposition§The juxtaposition is deliberate and slightly unkind.§这种**并置**是刻意的，也略带刻薄。
kinetic§Kinetic energy at that speed is what does the damage.§在那个速度下，造成破坏的是**动能**。
knack§There is a knack to opening the door without waking anyone.§开门而不吵醒任何人，是有**诀窍**的。
knowledgeable§Being knowledgeable about a period is not the same as understanding it.§**熟悉**一个时代与理解它不是一回事。
laconic§A laconic style hides how much was cut.§**简洁的**文风掩盖了删掉的分量。
lackadaisical§A lackadaisical afternoon is not the same as a rest.§**懒洋洋的**一个下午与休息不是一回事。
lament§The lament is sung once a year and by fewer people each time.§这支**哀歌**每年唱一次，唱的人一年比一年少。
languid§A languid river here becomes dangerous after rain.§这里**慵懒**的河流在雨后会变得危险。
languor§The languor of the reading room is its chief attraction.§阅览室里那份**倦懒**正是它最大的魅力。
lassitude§Lassitude after a long project is not laziness.§长项目之后的**乏力**不是懒惰。
latent§Latent heat is released when the vapour condenses.§蒸汽凝结时会释放**潜热**。
laud§He is lauded for a discovery two other people also made.§他因一项另外两人也做出的发现而**受赞誉**。
lavish§A lavish edition sold badly and is now worth a fortune.§一个**奢华**的版本当年卖得很差，如今价值不菲。
lavishly§They were lavishly entertained and learned nothing.§他们受到**盛情款待**，却什么也没了解到。
lax§Lax about deadlines and rigid about commas, he was hard to work with.§他在截止日期上**松散**，在逗号上苛刻，很难共事。
leery§Be leery of a result that arrives exactly on schedule.§对一个恰好按时到来的结果要**留心**。
legalize§Legalizing the path settled a hundred years of trespass.§把这条小路**合法化**，了结了一百年的擅闯之争。
legendary§The legendary founder may never have existed.§那位**传说**中的创立者可能根本不存在。
legitimacy§Legitimacy is granted by others and cannot be claimed.§**正当**性由他人赋予，无法自己宣称。
legitimate§A legitimate question deserves a real answer.§一个**正当**的问题应当得到真正的回答。
legitimize§Do not legitimize a bad practice by writing it into the manual.§不要把一种坏做法写进手册，从而让它**名正言顺**。
lengthy§After a lengthy silence he asked for the question again.§**长久的沉默**之后，他请对方把问题再说一遍。
leniency§She asked for leniency and offered to pay the cost.§她请求**从宽处理**，并提出承担费用。
lessen§Nothing lessens the shock of a familiar street rebuilt.§熟悉的街道被重建，那种震动无从**减轻**。
lethargy§Lethargy after lunch is a design problem, not a character flaw.§午后的**倦怠**是设计问题，不是性格缺陷。
levity§Levity at a funeral can be a form of tenderness.§葬礼上的**轻松**也可能是一种温柔。
levy§A levy on imported paper closed two small presses.§对进口纸张的**征税**关掉了两家小出版社。
lexicon§Every family has a private lexicon of about forty words.§每个家庭都有一套四十来个词的**私人词汇**。
liability§Limited liability changed what a company could risk.§有限**责任**改变了公司可以承担的风险。
libel§Libel law shapes what a biography can say about the living.§**诽谤**法决定了传记能怎样写在世的人。
liberality§The liberality of the reading room's hours saved her thesis.§阅览室开放时间的**宽松**救了她的论文。
libertine§He was called a libertine by people who envied him.§嫉妒他的人管他叫**浪子**。
licentious§What one century calls licentious the next calls candid.§一个世纪称之为**放肆**的，下个世纪称之为坦率。
likelihood§Likelihood is not the same as probability, though the words are traded.§**似然**与概率不是一回事，尽管两个词常被混用。
linchpin§Pull out the linchpin and the whole schedule falls apart.§抽掉这个**关键**，整个日程就散了。
linkage§The linkage transmits the motion without any electronics.§这套**连杆机构**不用任何电子元件就传递运动。
lionize§Do not lionize a scientist for a result that took a lab of thirty.§不要为一个三十人实验室的成果去**神化**一位科学家。
liquefy§Gas liquefies under pressure and takes a fraction of the space.§气体加压后**液化**，体积只剩一小部分。
lithe§A lithe young willow bends where an old one breaks.§**柔韧**的小柳树在老柳树折断的地方只是弯了弯。
litigious§A litigious atmosphere makes everyone write worse letters.§**好打官司**的氛围让所有人的信都写得更糟。
loathe§She loathes the word and uses it in every third paragraph.§她**厌恶**这个词，却每隔两段就用一次。
lobbyist§A lobbyist's best work is invisible in the final text.§**说客**最成功的工作，在最终文本里看不出来。
locution§The locution survives in one village and nowhere else.§这种**说法**只在一个村子里留存下来。
loftiness§There is a loftiness in the tone that the argument cannot support.§这种语气的**高远**，是论证支撑不住的。
lone§A lone dissenting note is recorded in the minutes.§会议记录里记下了**唯一一票**反对。
loner§Calling someone a loner is often a failure of curiosity.§把一个人称作**独行者**，往往是缺乏好奇心。
longevity§The longevity of a rumor depends on how useful it is.§一个谣言的**寿命**取决于它有多有用。
loquacious§A loquacious witness gives away more than a silent one.§**话多**的证人比沉默的证人泄露得更多。
lucid§He was lucid for an hour each morning and wrote then.§他每天早上有一小时**头脑清明**，就在那时写作。
lucrative§The least lucrative part of the business is the one worth keeping.§这门生意里**最不赚钱**的部分，恰恰是值得保留的。
ludicrous§What is ludicrous in one context is standard in another.§在一种语境里**荒唐**的事，在另一种语境里是常规。
lugubrious§A lugubrious cello opens the second act.§第二幕以一段**悲哀的**大提琴开场。
lullaby§The lullaby is in a minor key, which children never notice.§这首**摇篮曲**是小调，孩子从来不会注意到。
lurid§Lurid detail crowds out the one fact that matters.§**骇人**的细节挤掉了唯一要紧的事实。
lush§A lush description of a plain room tells you about the writer.§对一个简朴房间的**丰饶**描写，说明的是作者。
luxurious§A luxurious amount of time is the rarest luxury.§充裕的时间是最稀有的**奢侈**。
machination§No machination was needed; incompetence did the work.§用不着什么**阴谋**，无能就足够了。
magisterial§A magisterial tone can conceal a very ordinary argument.§**权威**的语气可以掩盖一个极其平常的论点。
magnanimity§Magnanimity costs the winner very little.§**宽宏大量**对胜者来说代价极小。
magnanimous§A magnanimous concession was read as weakness.§一次**宽宏**的让步被理解为软弱。
magnify§A lens magnifies the flaw along with everything else.§**放大**镜在放大一切的同时也放大了瑕疵。
magnitude§An earthquake of that magnitude occurs here twice a century.§这种**震级**的地震在这里每世纪发生两次。
mainstay§Volunteers were the mainstay of the whole operation.§志愿者是整个运作的**支柱**。
malfeasance§Malfeasance requires intent; incompetence does not.§**渎职**需要故意，无能则不需要。
mandate§The doctor's mandate does not extend to the patient's finances.§医生的**授权**不延伸到病人的财务。
mandatory§Helmets became mandatory the year after the accident.§事故发生后的第二年，头盔成了**强制要求**。
